Don’t waste your money on this guy. If google done half a star I would be hesitant to even give that.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and completely unacceptable service.

I took the time to complete Neocept’s consultation form in considerable detail so the meeting could be productive and efficient.

Despite this, the host arrived late and was clearly unprepared. It was obvious that very little, if any, of the information I had submitted had been reviewed.

Despite the poor start, I gave them the benefit of the doubt and decided to proceed. I received their quote and documents, completed everything immediately the following day, and confirmed that I wanted to move forward.

Three days later, I have effectively been ghosted despite three follow-up emails and a call to the office.

For a service based business, this level of communication is appalling. If you cannot or do not want to take on a client, simply say so. Ignoring someone who has invested their time, completed your paperwork and confirmed they want to proceed is incredibly disrespectful.

What makes this particularly disappointing is that the founder speaks about being passionate about supporting women owned businesses. As a woman myself, I experienced the complete opposite of that sentiment.

In a world dominated by blue chip companies and corporate giants, SMEs should be championing and supporting one another. At the absolute minimum, that means respecting each other’s time and effort. Basic communication, courtesy and professionalism should never be too much to expect.

I very rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience has caused completely unnecessary frustration and anxiety. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Neocept. A complete waste of my time.

one_star_reviews.text:
One Star — Absolutely Unacceptable

I have genuinely never had a hotel experience this appalling.

We arrived to find that our room had not been cleaned at all. The previous guests’ dirty bedding was still on the bed, tissues were left around the room, and the toilet was dirty. This wasn’t a minor oversight — the room had quite literally not been serviced. In addition to this, we heard other guests having the same issue as they complained at the same time we did.

Things somehow got even worse when we returned later. The room was 33°C, with absolutely no air conditioning. The windows had blockers fitted to them so they could only be opened by a tiny amount — not even enough to properly get your fingers through — meaning there was effectively no way to cool the room down.

We were eventually offered a fan in the middle of the night, after repeatedly going down to the reception and calling the mobile number multiple times, only to discover that the fan didn’t even work.

At that point, the room was so unbearably hot that we had no choice but to leave our room and sleep in the hotel lobby.

Let that sink in: we paid to stay in a hotel room and ended up sleeping in the lobby because the room was too hot to sleep in, after being given a room that hadn’t even been cleaned and a fan that didn’t work.

This wasn’t a slightly disappointing stay. It was an absolute failure from start to finish. Basic cleanliness, basic comfort and basic customer service were all completely lacking.

I would strongly advise anyone considering staying here to think twice. Paying for a hotel room should not mean having to clean up after previous guests, endure 33°C temperatures with no functioning way of cooling the room, and ultimately sleep in the lobby.

Quite possibly the worst hotel experience I’ve ever had. Avoid.

one_star_reviews.text:
We contacted Destination London in July to find an apartment before our return to school on September 1st, opting for their £1000 package (unlimited viewings) after reading all the glowing reviews. All the promises made to us turned out to be lies. We were promised support, viewings, communication… but in just one month, we only had four viewings, all filmed terribly (one of which was a video already made by another agency). None of the apartments met our criteria, which we had explicitly discussed during our initial call (especially the essentials, like budget, furnished, and two double bedrooms). We were shown apartments that weren't available at the end of August, were out of our budget, and only had one bedroom.

After several weeks of no clear communication and disrespect from the agent when we asked them to respect our criteria, we decided to contact them again for the umpteenth time. The result: they told us they didn't know it was an emergency and that we had to move in at the end of August… so we ended up sending them our own apartment viewings 🤡 In the end, the apartment they found for us was a last resort (since we had become completely desperate to avoid homelessness). Only one criterion was met: the budget (£2300 excluding bills). Obviously, there was no support with the paperwork; we had to communicate with the landlord's agent ourselves, so yet another empty promise about support until the signing. Since then, radio silence.

£1000 to subcontract our search to a London agency.

If we had to start our search from scratch, we would go directly to a local agency. Honestly, run away, the positive reviews are not representative of their service, if you can even call it that.

Had they bothered to inform us beforehand that the bus would be available, and given us the option to get a refund, we would have definitely opted out instead of wasting our afternoon.

Several unhappy passengers left mid tour, including us.

I do not recommend this tour at all. In fact I think it should be discontinued because of how bad it was. They were very disorganized, at one point the guide was telling us more about Mary Poppins and a very generic history of London instead of focusing on the movie.

I would strongly suggest avoiding this and instead finding your own way to the 2 locations instead.
Very disappointing for the children - not worth it at all.

Extremely concerning experience with Canary Wharf Group Residential. I would think very carefully before renting or buying a property managed by them.

At Ten Park Drive, I personally handed a prepaid Royal Mail parcel to the concierge for collection. It was accepted and clearly labelled, and Royal Mail had a confirmed collection and attended the building.

Instead, concierge staff opened my parcel without permission, went through my personal belongings, decided themselves that the contents “did not appear to be of clearly significant value”, and then disposed of everything — without contacting me once.

What is equally concerning is how CWG Residential handled the situation afterwards: no meaningful apology, no compensation, and no genuine accountability. Instead, I received defensive responses attempting to justify what happened, including claims about the Royal Mail collection that are contradicted by the documentary evidence I have.

This is not the standard I would expect from a company managing supposedly premium residential developments. It raises serious concerns about residents’ privacy and property, staff accountability, complaint handling and overall management standards.

Based on my experience, I would strongly caution anyone considering renting or buying in a property managed by Canary Wharf Group Residential.

I strongly recommend doing your own due diligence before paying Celebrity Booker.
I paid £75 for membership and a further £40 for a photoshoot which Celebrity Booker explicitly confirmed to me in writing “had been booked and was scheduled to take place at BBC Wales in Cardiff this Saturday.”
After finding a concerning review from another person relating to a purported photoshoot at the same location, I asked Celebrity Booker for information that would allow me to verify the booking independently.
I then contacted BBC Wales myself. I spoke directly to security, who checked and told me that my name was not booked in and that there was no external photoshoot booked. I have retained a recording of that conversation.
After I began questioning and independently verifying the arrangements, Celebrity Booker cancelled the photoshoot and subsequently terminated my membership.
They have stated in writing that they will refund my £40 photoshoot payment and £75 membership payment, totalling £115. At the time of writing, I have not received either refund. I will update this review if/when the money is received.
I have also raised the matter with a BBC Wales producer I have previously worked with. She has asked me to preserve my payment records and correspondence and has requested Celebrity Booker's contact details because the BBC is interested in pursuing the matter.
Everything stated in this review relates to my own experience and records I have retained.
My advice: verify everything independently before parting with money.

Extremely disappointing experience — felt more like a sales operation than healthcare.

I paid £69 for an X-ray, with what I considered to be questionable measurement methods afterwards. The whole assessment felt rushed and superficial.

The initial consultation was only around five minutes, yet I was apparently told exactly how many treatment sessions I needed. How can someone confidently determine a complete course of treatment after such a brief assessment?

Then came the sales process. To discuss payment, I was taken into a tiny separate room, where I felt pressured to commit to the recommended treatment package. I was even offered a promotion for paying upfront.

So I paid £69 for an X-ray, had an extremely brief assessment, was given a predetermined number of sessions, and was then taken aside into a small room to discuss payment — with an incentive to pay immediately.

That is not how I expected a healthcare appointment to feel. It felt heavily sales-driven from start to finish.

I would strongly recommend anyone considering this clinic not committing to a package or paying upfront during the appointment. Take the proposed treatment plan away, ask how they calculated the number of sessions, ask what the X-ray actually demonstrates, and get an independent opinion.

I would strongly advise anyone considering this company to look very carefully at the full cost and contractual terms before signing.

Over a three-year period, we have ended up paying approximately £15,000 for three phones, in addition to around £100 per month for the phone lines – and we do not even own the phones at the end of the agreement. Given our experience over three years, I can only sympathise with customers who have entered into much longer agreements.

Our experience of the sales and contracting process has also been extremely disappointing. We encountered several errors in the contracts which required repeated amendments. During this back-and-forth process, additional items and charges appeared within revised documentation, which made it very difficult to keep track of exactly what we were agreeing to.

We have also repeatedly had to ask for charges relating to services we do not use to be removed from our bills. In some cases, these charges have subsequently reappeared a few months later. If they are not spotted immediately, we have found that obtaining refunds for previous months is problematic.

Overall, I am extremely disappointed with our experience and genuinely shocked at the way the account has been managed. The phones themselves look good, but in my opinion they come nowhere close to justifying the overall cost and contractual arrangement.

Choosing this provider was a seriously poor business decision on my part, and I would not recommend them.

Finally, if another telecommunications provider happens to read this review, please do not contact us offering to switch our service. After this experience, we will only consider dealing directly with a mainstream provider in future.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’ve been having my upper lip waxed for years and unfortunately had a very poor experience here. Strip wax was applied considerably beyond the area I expected to be treated, leaving me with painful, linear grazes/skin lifting extending out from both sides of my mouth. More than 24 hours later the marks remain clearly visible, as shown in the photos.

I emailed the salon immediately after the appointment with photographs but received no response, so I went back in person. I was disappointed that, rather than acknowledging the injury and apologising, I was told that this was a normal reaction covered by the salon’s terms and conditions, that I had consented to it, and that the areas affected were considered part of the “upper lip”. Clearly not.

I appreciate that temporary redness can occur after waxing — I have been waxed regularly for many years and am familiar with that. These linear grazes are not my usual post-wax redness, they are skin abrasions and the person doing the treatment would have seen them (I was not offered a mirror). I was particularly disappointed by the way my concern was handled when I returned to the salon, especially the suggestion that I simply cover the grazes with make up.

UPDATE FOLLOWING THE SALON’S RESPONSE:

The salon’s response does not represent what happened fairly. I did give the salon an opportunity to address this directly. I emailed photographs of the injury shortly after the appointment and, having received no response, returned to the salon in person the following day specifically to discuss what had happened.

The fact that I did not raise concerns before leaving the original appointment is because I had not seen the injury at that point. There was no mirror available and I did not see what had happened to my skin until I got home. Over the following hours, the marks became increasingly apparent as clearly visible, sore grazes, as shown in the photograph.

When I returned to discuss this directly, I was told that this was a normal/possible reaction to waxing, that skin lifting/grazing was covered by the terms and conditions I had agreed to, and that the marks extending across my cheeks were considered to be within the “upper lip” treatment area. I found this response dismissive and did not consider the matter resolved.

I did decline aloe vera when I returned to the salon. By then I was already caring for the damaged skin myself. I don’t think declining an offer of aloe vera has any bearing on whether the treatment should have caused the injury in the first place.

I am also disappointed by the suggestion in the salon’s response that I should find somewhere “more suitable for my needs”. My “needs” here were entirely ordinary: to have a routine upper-lip wax, a treatment I have had regularly for many years, without being left with grazes extending across both cheeks.

I had been a regular customer since 2024 and had previously been happy with the salon. That is precisely why I contacted them privately and then took the trouble to return in person before leaving this review. What prompted the negative review was not only the injury itself, but the way my concerns were handled when I raised them.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, my experience at Terapi Londra was extremely disappointing, and I did not find the environment or the approach suitable for my child.

The clinic itself did not feel appropriate for children’s therapy. The room we were in was very small, with large furniture leaving very little space for a child to move or engage in activities. I also found the room poorly ventilated and, in my opinion, not sufficiently child-friendly. There was also a tall shelf with multiple objects on it which appeared unstable, and some items nearly fell onto my son. While I was there I have checked all the rooms and all of them were very small.

More seriously, I had a very upsetting experience during the therapy session with Özge Öztürk. After my son had been in the small room for around an hour, I opened the door so that I could change his nappy and offer him some water. The therapist became angry and shouted at me in front of my son. I was also accused of lying about changing his nappy, which I found extremely upsetting and inappropriate.

At another point, when my son was bored and wanted to leave the room, I felt that his arm was grabbed and he was pulled towards the room. I was very uncomfortable with this interaction.

In terms of the actual therapy, I personally did not see a clear structure, meaningful activities or advice tailored to my son’s individual needs. Much of the session appeared to involve my son trying to crawl around the small room between large chairs and a table, rather than engaging in activities that were appropriate or appealing for a young child.

Following the session, I contacted the management because of how upset I was about what had happened. I was initially told that I would receive a refund and that they were sorry and upset that we had been treated this way. However, this was later reversed, and I was told that they did not believe that these things had happened.

This was particularly disappointing after I had been led to believe that the matter would be resolved.

I have recordings relating to the incident and the session and  given the seriousness of my concerns, I intend to raise the matter with the appropriate professional and regulatory bodies.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic for a young child.

I've faced a rollercoaster of issues since going to the ADHD health clinic.
From my initial appointment, the Dr seemed to not be interested in any way in my diagnosis or experience, with all of my appointments being less than 10 minutes long, being charged hundreds of pounds a session.
After my first appointment I was asked to leave a 5* google review, which I'm glad I didn't do.

I was told what I would be prescribed and when I went to go and collect my medication (after they forgot to send my prescription so I had to chase this), they had sent the incorrect prescription and dose to the chemist.

On other occasions they only sent half the prescriptions, I've had last minute cancellations (I understand that these things happen, but added to the stress of the situation).

I was told at the start of the treatment to check with my GP that they accept shared care, which they told me they did. Only to reach the end of my treatment to be told regulations have changed and they can no longer work with certain private clinics - unsurprisingly this was never mentioned by the ADHD health clinic, nor did they offer any support - just tried to charge me £75 for each repeat prescription, before even sending my last medication after my £200 appointment.

I've had to chase and follow up medication on multiple occasions, ended up without medication on more times that I care to shed light on.

On the occasions when I have been able to get through to the reception team they are very lovely, and to their credit, have actioned things quickly. However I have called many times, been sent to voice mail, left voice mails for call backs which have never come.

For the amount of money I have spent on this service I am truely appalled and the only way I can fathom their 5* rating is due to them asking customers to review before they have allowed for any of these issues to occur.

one_star_reviews.text:
Firstly the appointment started slightly later than the alloted time. Dr. Zadeh was nice enough, however on several occasions I needed to correct what he'd written as my answer as it wasn't what I'd said, making me think there was just a 'script' being followed rather than a full engaged assessment.

**update**
After having had 6mths working with this centre, I can categorically say that they are not worth the money. Their organisational capability is so low and useless, it's beyond words. Having had a consultation with the clinician at the end of August, and emailing specific instructions about the prescription, I am still waiting (as of 12th October), for them to send the prescription! No apologies from any of the people, their conceitedness is incredible. The only time they are efficient is when they're asking for payment, for the rest, they're a complete joke.

I'd advise strongly against using their services, particularly if your condition means you need the medication to function daily, as they simply cannot organise anything. NOT RECOMMENDED AT ALL

I was unsure as to whether the business generally leans towards giving diagnosis, even if there are borderline answers, simply because it's private and there's money to be made.

However, despite all, the assessment was professional in manner, not particularly engaging, but okay. I don't know how it would differ, if at all, should I have had an in-person assessment, or one via the NHS, but my feeling is, given the consultants work for the NHS, that it would be the same. In which case, the main benefit of the ADHD centre is speed.

I really would not recommend the ADHD Centre AT ALL.

My first assessment was led by a psychiatrist who came across as completely disinterested and, in my experience, had an outdated understanding of ADHD, particularly how it can present in women and how symptoms can be masked or internalised.

The assessment was a very negative experience. I became overwhelmed by the sheer number of questions being thrown at me, but this was largely ignored. He didn’t appear to have read the extensive forms that I had completed beforehand, explained very little, and when I struggled to answer a question about my childhood, responded: “Well, if you don’t know, I don’t know either.”

The administration was equally frustrating. I was repeatedly chased for old school reports despite explaining several times that I no longer had them, and no one seemed to record the information I provided.

My eventual report was littered with mistakes and, more seriously, contained private information about third parties that I had specifically asked not to be included. The psychiatrist had agreed to this and told me I could request information to be removed, but subsequently refused to make amendments to the report.

I complained to the ADHD Centre and, after investigating, they apologised and offered me a reassessment. So I went through the entire process for a second time.

The shared-care issue has been even more frustrating. Before paying for a private assessment, I expressly asked about shared care and was told that most GPs, although not all, would accept it. That has not been my experience. My GP surgery will not accept private ADHD shared care, and my GP has since told me that the majority of GPs now do not accept these arrangements, partly because of the rapid increase in ADHD assessments and concerns about the quality of some private assessments. I have been unable to find a GP in my borough willing to accept one.

Had I been given an accurate and up-to-date picture when I specifically asked, I would not have chosen this route. After paying privately and going through two assessments, I am now having to undergo a THIRD assessment through Right to Choose to access treatment through a route my GP surgery will accept.

Finally, having now experienced the assessment process with a different clinic - and completed an adult ADHD informant form for a friend - I can see just how poor the ADHD Centre’s system is by comparison.

You are sent around eight lengthy forms asking for an enormous amount of information, much of which forms the basis of the final report. The assessment is recorded and, given the apparent use of AI alongside the information already supplied, it can feel as though you are doing a significant amount of the work yourself.

The forms are sent separately by email, all look virtually identical and disappear once submitted. There is no proper portal where you can see what you’ve completed, what remains outstanding or review your responses. For a service specifically designed for people with ADHD, asking patients to keep track of numerous lengthy forms scattered across separate emails seems particularly poorly thought through.

The whole experience was exhausting, frustrating and unnecessarily stressful.

We took our car in to repair a puncture.  The woman who met with us was off hand, despite an appointment made ahead of time. She acted like our custom was an interruption to her day and smoked while our grandson (a toddler) stood there.  It made us feel uncomfortable and so we went to Halfords.  It was a hard decision as we have always used Speedy Fit in the past and feel it is important to support local business - but not if the experience is unpleasant.

I approached NHS mental health services because I was already at an extremely difficult point in my life. Somehow, dealing with this Trust managed to make an already awful situation worse.

Eventually I made a formal complaint, and the Trust's own investigation acknowledged multiple shortcomings in how things had been communicated and handled.

You would think that might result in being treated with some humanity afterwards. Instead, even the complaints process has repeatedly made me feel like I am standing in a courtroom having to explain, justify and prove my mental health to the very organisation I approached because I was mentally unwell.
That is the part I find almost impossible to comprehend. Mental health patients are not professional case managers. When somebody tells you they are overwhelmed, struggling and finding it difficult even to engage with the process, the answer should not be to pile more process, deadlines and evidential burden onto them.

I feel totally and utterly let down by the NHS. I sought help and ended up more anxious, more distressed and far less trusting of mental health services than when I began.

I genuinely regret reaching out to them in the first place. A mental health service should never leave somebody feeling that way.

A dark blotch on the state of mental health in the NHS England, absolutely pitch dark.

I genuinely don’t know where to start with how disappointing my experience with this dealership has been.

We were the easiest customers they could have asked for. We viewed it, decided we wanted it and bought it for cash within the hour, as well as paying separately for an extended warranty. We collected the car as planned on 17 March.

Unfortunately, that was about as good as the experience got.

After just over a month, it became obvious the AC wasn’t working properly. We reported this and were told it may not have been properly tested because the car had been checked in a cold garage during winter. If you’re selling a car, “it was cold when we checked it” is hardly reassuring.

There was also a parking ticket from a previous owner covering the VIN number when we bought the car. We asked for this to be removed, and it was concerning that this hadn’t been noticed when the car arrived from auction.

The car was taken in and we were told the compressor had failed and needed replacing. After several days, we were told it was ready. I drove 7 miles home and the AC still didn’t work. It was blowing hot air and hadn’t clicked in once. The parking ticket covering the VIN hadn’t been removed.

When I called Chris, I was spoken to in an extremely patronising manner and repeatedly told it must be “user error”, including being asked whether I had actually pressed the AC button. I am perfectly capable of operating a AC system. The attitude was so dismissive that I eventually had to put my father on the phone. Interestingly, the conversation became noticeably more professional once a man was speaking.

The dealership then came to look at the car, describing this as a “gesture of goodwill”. They were there for approximately five minutes, removed the parking ticket and said the AC was working. I then drove for around an hour and a half, during which it worked for roughly two minutes before failing again.

Once again, I was told it was user error. As a female customer, being repeatedly spoken to in this way was incredibly insulting and patronising. I should not have to put a male relative on the phone to receive basic professionalism and respect.

There was also the issue of the extended warranty we had paid for separately. The air conditioning fault was reported within the dealership’s initial three-month warranty period, yet the compressor was ultimately dealt with using our separately purchased extended warranty. We were not asked for permission to use it.

The dealership then had the car again to investigate the fault. They kept it for two days without contacting us, and from then onwards communication became a complete battle. We repeatedly had to chase for updates, my dad had to email and phone numerous times, and we even had to visit the dealership in person to get answers. We were repeatedly told there was no update and they were waiting for parts.

I understand that cars go wrong and parts can take time. What I don’t understand is why the customer has to repeatedly chase a dealership for basic information about their own car.

The dealership had our car for 43 days between 17 March and 25 July. We had owned it for approximately 130 days. That means the dealership had our car for roughly one third of the entire time we had owned it.

When we raised concerns about this, we were essentially told it was “normal practice” and that these things can happen.

If having a customer’s car for 43 out of its first 130 days is their definition of normal, I would strongly suggest anyone considering buying from them thinks carefully.

The email correspondence from Chris was also extremely disappointing, with responses that were at times defensive, angry and unprofessional when we expressed our frustration.

I have kept the emails and voicemails relating to this entire situation.

As a female be careful if you’re considering buying from this dealership. Being spoken down to, having your knowledge questioned and repeatedly being told an obvious mechanical problem is “user error” is not acceptable customer service.

We attended the appointment and were told the report would be sent over in 4-6 weeks. After waiting 9 weeks with no communication, I contacted Laura to ask for an update. English Translation

In the Name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

O Allah, my Lord and my Master, You know my condition, You know what is in my heart, and You know my oppression and my pain.

O Allah, I am Your servant who has been wronged, and I am among the mustaḍʿafīn, the oppressed and downtrodden. You are my Protector, my Helper, and You are sufficient for me.

O Allah, I complain to You about what I have experienced in some mosques: poor treatment, hurt, and distress.

In some mosques I have encountered some imams, worshippers, and believers who outwardly wear religious clothing, grow beards, and display the symbols of religion, yet from some of them I have experienced arrogance, pride, and looking down upon me.

I have experienced some treating me with contempt and belittling me, looking at me as though they are better than me, higher than me, and closer to Allah than me. They have made their religious appearance, clothing, and beards seem like a reason to consider themselves superior to Your servants.

O Allah, I ask You: Is this what Your religion teaches? Is this the character of the mosque? Is this what Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad taught? Did You command Your servants to despise one another and to become arrogant toward one another?

Or is Your religion a religion of humility, mercy, justice, and beautiful character?

O Allah, You know how deeply this has hurt me, how it has wounded my heart, and how it has made me feel like a stranger and unwelcome in some of Your houses.

O Allah, do not let the bad character of some people become a reason for me to distance myself from You. Do not let the behaviour of some religious people become a reason for me to hate Your religion or distance myself from Your Messenger and his Ahl al-Bayt.

O Allah, show me Your religion as it truly is. Show me its mercy, its justice, and the beauty of its character.

O Allah, guide those who have wronged me, reform those who have mistreated me, restore my rights if I have been wronged, and help me through truth without making me unjust toward anyone else.

O Allah, mend what is broken within me, heal my wounds, relieve my distress, remove my worries and sadness, and grant me tranquillity and peace.

O Allah, keep me firm upon the truth. Do not let me abandon Your religion because of the mistakes of its followers, and do not let me judge Islam solely through the bad actions of some Muslims.

O Allah, be the Protector and Helper of the oppressed and the mustaḍʿafīn. Give me a way out of every hardship and relief from every worry.

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad. Keep me firm upon the Wilāyah of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, make me among those who hold firmly to them, those who hold firmly to Your rope, and those guided to Your Straight Path.

Āmīn, O Lord of the worlds.

one_star_reviews.text:
Wish it could be 0 stars. The only 1 star is for the reception staff, who are at least polite. Even standing outside on the street, you can constantly hear screaming and crying echoing from the unit. Walking inside, the environment is profoundly distressing, and it is painfully obvious that patients are actively declining mentally due to sheer negligence, something I know firsthand from witnessing it with my own eyes, hearing it happen while on the phone, and being told it directly by my loved one who is sadly stuck on that unit.

​The culture among staff is dismissive, punitive, and entirely devoid of empathy. Basic confidentiality and trust are routinely breached, leaving patients with no safe way to voice concerns or seek outside help without facing blowback. Concerns raised by loved ones are brushed aside, and families are kept at arm's length by rigid, consultant-dictated visiting restrictions that cut vulnerable patients off from their support systems when they need them most. To make matters worse, staff actively weaponize family involvement—even using loved ones as leverage or "bait" to enforce compliance, rather than prioritizing the patient's well-being.

​Treatment here is completely counterproductive. Staff are entirely unequipped to provide proper meal support, and instead of helping patients through meals, they resort to victim-blaming—telling individuals fighting severe eating disorders that they "only have themselves to blame" when interventions like nasogastric tubes become necessary. When NG feeds are forced, staff rely on heavy-handed, aggressive physical restraints performed incorrectly, frequently leaving patients bruised and physically harmed. To make matters worse, staff fail so completely in their duties that vulnerable patients are left to support and comfort each other through their breakdowns—an entirely unacceptable dynamic when everyone there is intensely unwell and fighting their own battles. Weight management is weaponized as a tool for punishment rather than part of a holistic recovery framework, completely ignoring the psychological reality of the illness.

​This place is entirely unfit for purpose and needs to be shut down immediately. If you or anyone you care about is fighting an eating disorder, do not send them to Ellern Mede Barnet. These individuals deserve a facility focused on actual safety and mental healthcare, not a toxic system that punishes patients for being ill.

one_star_reviews.text:
It’s recommended to call the crisis line in a crisis. Be aware that the staff will decide within 3 minutes if you are in crisis or not. There is no scope for recognising the individuality of emotions and how the presentation of a crisis can be diverse.

The lack of patience/compassion demonstrated if you’ve unfortunately had to call more than a few times because your assigned daytime team are not providing their basic duty of care is concerning.

The MH system may be on its knees and fair enough the crisis line receives a lot of calls’ but that’s no excuse for professionals to lack any basic compassion’ being able to end a call with gentleness and provision of signposting to alternative services should be a gentle experience because the person calling for ‘help’ may really benefit from that brief interaction. Even if a service user is not happy about the call having to end’ at least they won’t leave the call spiralling over the attitude of the person they spoke to and feeling like a burden on services they felt vulnerable enough to call.

Worst mental health experience of my life and they are refusing to do a transfer and still contacting me even though they are not suppose to avoid at all cost they should be shut down in now have to go through legal proceedings I have made a serious complaint with pals and my gp surgery and they are still contacting me even though they are not suppose to

If zero stars were an option, that is what I would give. Is it really acceptable for a mental health department to disregard the views and firsthand experience of a family who have lived with and cared for a relative with schizophrenia for over 20 years? Family insight was not properly sought or considered, while accusations made by the patient appeared to be accepted without adequately establishing the facts. Even more disappointing was the failure to provide clear answers to direct questions raised through the PALS process. A deeply disappointing and, in our experience, disgraceful standard of care.

I had a phone call the other day stating my initial assessment would be on 25/08 at 930am but I had several missed calls today (21/08) claiming my appointment was today at 915am. When I was called I made sure to confirm the date for this several times and the lady seem annoyed that I kept asking but I wanted to double check so it feels like I'd been lied to. I did a long shift at work last night which was honestly awful but I then couldn't sleep after so by the point of them calling id had 2 hours sleep maximum. I called greenwich hub in a very emotional state because this isn't the first time this has happened with mental health services and another lady picked up the phone who honestly didn't sound as if she cared at all and rushed to get me off the phone as if she didnt want to deal with issues like that today. Again, just rude. I'm 100% missing out some bits here which if anything will just make it sound worse but im just exhausted. If you can get anything from this, yes, I am saying that I dont think you should go to greenwich hub for mental health issues as it just feels like a mockery.

Edit:
Upon having my telephone assessment I recieved a NHSmail letter to my email with the details of the report which I 100% believe are false. I am currently taking this up with the oxleas complaint team so hopefully theyre able to do something. GMHH have severely let me down from the moment I turned to them. I had to call the oxleas crisis line and the same lady who lied on the report called me back making it feel like a joke and as if they don't care at all.

Further Edit:
In January 2024 (after my incident with the mental health hub who told me there was nothing wrong with me) I was placed with a crisis intervention team who gave me a diagnosis for my mental health. After I finished with the crisis intervention team I have been placed back with the mental health hub who have had to take my mental health seriously following a recent suicide attempt. Special thanks to Robin from greenwich mental health hub.

I have had issues time and time again with this service my previous time with this service was a much better experience but I have once again been let down.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went to see Mr Adrian Lower today after choosing him based on the reviews I had read and the impression that he has experience dealing with complex cases. Unfortunately, I left feeling quite disappointed and unsupported.I had to wait nearly 45 minutes for my appointment, only to feel that my notes and previous information had not been properly reviewed beforehand. I was grateful that I had brought up the fact that there was a disc from my MRI, but I felt that this should have been requested and reviewed before my appointment, particularly given the complexity of my case.
I was also disappointed that I was not scanned, especially as I had understood that a scan would be part of the appointment. I travelled quite a distance for this appointment and if I had known that I was essentially coming in just to discuss my case without being examined or scanned, I could have had the consultation online and avoided the time and expense of travelling.
What disappointed me most was that I did not feel I was given an opportunity to properly explore the non-invasive options that may be available in my case. My understanding is that there may be a procedure that could reduce the fibroid without having the same impact on my life as major surgery. I would have appreciated being given a chance of the non invasive procedure,one until it’s tried

I also explained that my fertility clinic has told me they could potentially have a frozen embryo ready, and that once the fibroid had been treated, the intention could be to proceed with embryo transfer. I wanted this possibility to be discussed as part of the overall plan, but I did not feel that this was really listened to or explored.

I appreciate that a specialist may not agree that a particular treatment is suitable, but I believe patients should be given the opportunity to explore and try especially if it’s not going to impact on life.

Another part of the consultation that I found particularly disappointing was being advised to consider adoption from Nigeria. I understand that adoption may be an option for some people, but I was surprised by this suggestion, particularly when I had travelled to see a specialist to discuss my medical situation and the possible treatment options available to me. I would have expected my fertility goals and the treatment options available to me to be explored more fully before being directed towards adoption abroad. I also wondered why Nigeria was specifically suggested rather than adoption options here in the UK.

Overall, I left feeling that the appointment had been a waste of both my time and money. I travelled there because I genuinely hoped that, given his experience with complex cases, I would receive a more thorough assessment and a clear discussion of my options. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed and shocked by the way Shila treated my friend.

My friend was expecting her to represent him in an upcoming court case. He had been assured that the firm would apply for Legal Aid and, relying on this, he waited for them to progress his case.

He sent Shila several emails asking questions directly related to his case, including asking for legal advice and whether he could provide additional information for his witness statement. Instead of addressing his questions, she decided to stop acting for him and told him to find another solicitor, with only around two weeks remaining before his court hearing.

My friend repeatedly asked her not to drop his case and explained how difficult it would be for him to find alternative representation at such short notice. He also explained that he was currently on sick leave following a recent head injury and was suffering from severe anxiety and depression.

Despite being made aware of his circumstances, Shila responded that she was sorry to hear about his health but would not represent him, that there would be no further replies, and wished him all the best.

I was genuinely shocked by this response. In my view, this showed an extraordinary lack of sensitivity towards a client who was clearly distressed and facing an imminent court hearing.

The most upsetting part is that my friend had relied on assurances that his Legal Aid application and representation were being dealt with. Valuable time was therefore lost while he waited, only for the case to be dropped at very short notice after he asked questions about his own case.

The additional stress caused by suddenly being left without representation so close to the hearing has had a significant impact on his wellbeing.

I simply cannot understand why asking reasonable questions about your own case should result in a client being left to find another solicitor at such short notice. Based on what I witnessed, I found the way this situation was handled deeply upsetting and extremely unprofessional.

one_star_reviews.text:
What an absolutely incredible experience getting my SIA badge. I’ve never had to provide so much evidence that I am, in fact, a real human being.
Getting an SIA badge isn't simply saying, “Hello, my name is Dave and I'd like to work in security.”
Oh no.
You apparently need enough identification to convince everyone that you didn't just materialise in a Travelodge car park three weeks ago.
Passport? Driving licence? Proof of address? Employment history? Training certificates?
At one point I genuinely expected them to ask for DNA, blood type and photographic evidence of myself existing between 2003 and 2007.
I was waiting for:
“Can you provide the exact circumference of the orange your great-grandfather ate on Tuesday, 14th June 1966?”
Sorry, no idea.
“How many seeds were inside it?”
I’ll have to contact the family archives.
“Can you provide photographic evidence of the pigeon that flew into your uncle's window in 1987?”
Unfortunately, the pigeon died before smartphones were invented.
“How many feathers did it have?”
Approximately 4,731. I can provide a witness statement from my aunt if required.
And God forbid you've moved house. Suddenly you're expected to reconstruct your entire residential history like you're being investigated by MI5.
“Where did you live?”
Here.
“And before that?”
There.
“And before that?”
Also there.
“And before that?”
Look mate, I was 11. I was mostly interested in Pokémon.
Then comes the course.
One of the basic requirements for working in security is having a basic understanding of English and being able to operate a radio.
Sounds reasonable.
Until you sit in the classroom and realise that for some people, English appears to be an optional DLC.
The trainer asks:
“Can everyone understand me?”
Silence.
Someone is staring at the radio like it's an alien artefact.
The instructor explains a simple procedure.
Five minutes later:
“Sorry mate, what we doing?”
Mate. He literally just explained it. With PowerPoint. And pictures.
Then comes radio training.
“Go ahead.”
CLICK
“Yeah, I'm here.”
CLICK
“Can you hear me?”
CLICK
“Hello?”
CLICK
“Is this thing working?”
At this point you're wondering whether you're on a security course or an expedition to recover the lost technology of Atlantis.
Instructor:
“Press the button before speaking.”
Radio operator:
“Yeah, okay.”
PRESS
“Yeah, can you hear me?”
RELEASES BUTTON
“OVER.”
The trainer looks like he's reconsidering every decision that led him here.
Then:
“Can you give me your location?”
“I'm in the building.”
Brilliant. We've narrowed it down to approximately 40,000 square feet.
And somehow, despite all this, people still receive security badges.
I genuinely think the SIA should take the process further.
Before issuing a badge, applicants should have to provide:
Their great-grandfather's favourite biscuit.
The exact circumference of his orange.
The number of feathers on the pigeon that hit their uncle's window.
Three references from people who witnessed said pigeon.
A full history of every house they've ever entered.
Confirmation of whether they can identify the correct end of a radio.
A notarised statement confirming they understand the phrase “Can you hear me?”
Joking aside, security is obviously important and proper vetting is necessary. But the contrast is hilarious: you can spend weeks proving your identity, providing documents and completing training, only to watch someone struggle with basic English and radio communication and still walk away with the same badge.
Overall: 10/10 for bureaucracy, 11/10 for entertainment.
Would recommend.
Just remember to bring your passport, driving licence, proof of address, employment history, training certificates, your great-grandfather's orange measurements, the pigeon census and, most importantly...
LEARN HOW TO USE THE BLOODY RADIO.

I took my miniature Dachshund here last week to have her claws clipped. Her nails are very dark, and I specifically chose to have them done professionally because I was nervous about accidentally cutting into the quick myself.

Unfortunately, the groomer attempted to lift my Dachshund onto the grooming table by picking her up underneath her front legs, without supporting her back. As a Dachshund owner, I found this particularly concerning given the breed’s susceptibility to back problems.

To make matters worse, one of her nails was clipped too short and she was left bleeding. This was extremely distressing for both my dog and me. What I found particularly upsetting was the complete lack of apology or empathy afterwards. I was still charged the full amount for the service.

I subsequently spoke to the owners because I felt it was important to make them aware of what had happened. Rather than receiving an apology or any acknowledgement of how upsetting the experience had been, I was simply told that it is difficult to see the quick when a dog has dark nails. I was already fully aware of this — it is precisely why I took her to a professional in the first place.

Accidents can happen, but it is the way they are handled afterwards that says a lot about a business. I would have expected some basic concern for my dog’s wellbeing and, at the very least, an apology.

I have been a regular customer of the pet shop and used to visit every weekend, which makes this even more disappointing. Sadly, after this experience, I will not be returning.

The lack of care, empathy and accountability shown towards my dog was extremely upsetting. I would strongly encourage other dog owners to consider this before trusting them with their pets

one_star_reviews.text:
We had an extremely disappointing experience with Brown & Co Estate Agents during the end of our tenancy.

They tried to claim a substantial amount from my deposit for issues that were entirely unreasonable, including the removal of an item of furniture that actually belonged to the property owner, alleged missing lightbulbs, and professional cleaning charges for the entire property including carpets that were nearly 20 years old and beyond life expectancy. Many of the deductions appeared to be aimed at improving the property for the landlord to sell, rather than fairly addressing genuine tenant wear and tear. It was particularly concerning that some of the extra items and the amount of money being claimed were added to throughout the process. The claims presented before and during the DPS dispute process were not entirely consistent, which raised questions about the validity of some of the deductions being sought.

Throughout the dispute, Josh Bailey's communication was often awkward with no negotiation skills, and there was a clear attempt to pursue claims for betterment rather than what was fair and reasonable under tenancy deposit rules. Rather than acting as an impartial agent, it seemed there was a deliberate focus on maximising the return to the landlord.

We were also disappointed by his handling of a small area of mould around the faulty hob extractor fan, as the problem was not addressed fairly or appropriately.

Fortunately, the Deposit Protection Service (DPS) reviewed the evidence independently and saw through many of the claims being made. The adjudicator recognised that the property had not been professionally cleaned when we moved in and rejected a significant proportion of the deductions being sought from our deposit.

Overall, the experience left us with little confidence in Brown & Co's ability to deal fairly and objectively with tenants. My advice to anyone renting through this agency would be to take extensive photographs at check-in and check-out, keep detailed records of all communication, and not be afraid to challenge deposit deductions through the DPS if you believe they are unfair.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Brown & Co Estate Agents.

I am extremely disappointed with how Farnborough College of Technology handled my son’s application for admission to the A-Level programme.

My son previously studied Engineering at the college and was permitted to withdraw from his T-Level after being advised by college staff. When we subsequently discussed his intention to return and pursue A-Levels, we were not clearly informed that completing the first year of the T-Level, maintaining specific attendance levels, or demonstrating particular behavioural improvements would be conditions for future admission.

Despite submitting his A-Level application months in advance, the concerns regarding his previous attendance, behaviour and engagement were only used to refuse his admission at a very late stage, just days before the new academic year. Had these concerns and the possibility of refusal been communicated when his application was submitted, he would have had a reasonable opportunity to apply elsewhere.

What is particularly disappointing is that the college now refers to conditions that we do not believe were clearly communicated to us at the time. The college also states that its decision is based on his previous record, yet this was not communicated to us during the application process until the very end.

I fully accept that colleges have the right to assess whether a student is suitable for a programme. However, students and parents also deserve clear communication, consistency and sufficient notice to make alternative educational arrangements.

I hope the college reviews its approach to cases like this and improve the communication practices so that other students and families are not placed in the same difficult position.

My son is now doing A level in a different college.

My whole family have been wanting to go here for ages but do to one person needing lactose free food and another coeliac we were hesitant. We finally went to find that they had almost no options for people with any other kind of dietary requirements and the few options they did have were unpalatable. It's not hard to do amazing gluten free or vegan desserts anymore and have them available for those who need it. Up your game dessert shop and be more inclusive of those who struggle enough to eat out and enjoy life as it is.

I contacted LBC around three weeks ago because I needed to arrange a box order for delivery outside London, as I am based in Oxford.

During my initial call, I was told that my request would be forwarded to the appropriate team and that I should wait for them to contact me. I was also told that the minimum order was 2 medium boxes. At no point was I told that I would need to pay a deposit.

A week later, I called again to follow up and was told the same thing — that my request had been forwarded and I should wait. Another week passed, so I followed up again and received essentially the same response.

I have now contacted another customer service team by email, only to be told that I actually need to pay a deposit for every box and that the minimum order is 3 medium boxes.

This is incredibly frustrating. I don't mind being told what the actual requirements are, but I do expect consistent and accurate information from customer service. If I had been given the correct information during my first call, I could have made the necessary arrangements three weeks ago.

I need my parcels to arrive by December, and these repeated delays and contradictory responses are now putting my plans at risk.

The biggest issue for me is not even the additional requirements — it is the lack of communication, the repeated need to chase for updates, and receiving completely different information from different representatives

Since December 2025 I m calling for sending two boxes to Philippines I carryon calling every week and the first time they said the coming to collecting the next day,
I took a day’s off from work at 5 pm they still didn’t come I phoned the office and the lady said they are available till 9 pm but no one come to collect tham
The  boxes are still here at home ready to go. I’m still phoning them but not luck.
Horrible service .

one_star_reviews.text:
Review

STAY WELL AWAY FROM THIS PLACE! The way they treat loyal customers is absolutely disgusting. I’ve been with them from day one, yet apparently that means absolutely nothing to them. They repeatedly increase their prices without any proper warning or consideration, and then treat you like you’re just another number.

It honestly feels like all they care about is squeezing more money out of people rather than having any respect for the customers who have supported them from the beginning. Loyalty clearly means nothing to them.

After being treated like this, I have absolutely no intention of continuing to give them my money. If you value being treated with respect and being given proper notice when prices change, STAY AWAY.

Vincent,

I completely disagree with your version of events, and I think you are deliberately missing the point of my complaint.

My issue was never that you increased the price of an appointment that was already in the diary. My issue was the way the increase was communicated and implemented. You may have emailed clients, but giving notice that a price increase is happening is not the same as giving loyal customers a reasonable opportunity to book additional appointments at the previous price before the increase took effect. If you knew about the increase in advance, there was absolutely nothing stopping you from giving customers proper notice and a clear window in which to book at the existing rate.

Saying that the increase was “necessary” because of rising costs also does not change how you chose to communicate it. Every business faces rising costs, but that does not excuse poor communication or mean loyal customers should simply accept an immediate price increase without having an opportunity to plan for it.

Your comparison with other salons is also beside the point. I am not complaining about whether you are cheaper or more expensive than ten other salons. I am complaining about how you treated a customer who has supported you from day one. You seem far more interested in defending the percentage increase than actually acknowledging why a loyal customer would be annoyed by the way it was handled.

As for the reviews, I stand by my criticism of the experience and the way this situation has been handled. I accept that I only personally used the Kentish Town salon, and I am happy for you to remove any reviews you believe were inappropriate for locations I did not visit. But that does not invalidate the underlying complaint about the business or the way I have been treated as a long-standing customer.

What I find particularly disappointing is that, rather than acknowledging why I was upset and trying to resolve the situation, your response has largely been to defend the business and tell me why my criticism is wrong. That only reinforces my view that customer loyalty is not being valued in the way I would expect.

I have now decided to take my business elsewhere. That is a direct consequence of how this has been handled, not simply because prices have increased. A price increase can be perfectly reasonable; the way you communicate and implement it is equally important.

I wish you and the team well, but after being a loyal customer from day one, I am extremely disappointed that this is how the relationship has ended.
